newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan accepts resignation of U.N. Cyprus envoy.
newsitem.headline: Annan accepts resignation of U.N. Cyprus envoy.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan has accepted the resignation of his special representative for Cyprus, Professor Han Sung-joo, and will seek a replacement, a U.N. spokesman said on Monday.

Han, a former South Korean foreign minister and a professor of political science at Korea University, has told Annan that, due to other pressing commitments, he would be unable to continue in the U.N. post beyond April 30, the spokesman said.
The United Nations has been trying for decades to reunite the divided Mediterranean island under a federal system.

Han is currently visiting Cyprus to try to arrange the first face-to-face meeting in nearly three years between President Glafcos Clerides, as head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.

"The secretary-general has accepted Professor Han's decision with much regret and expressed his warm appreciation for the dedicated work he had carried out in the last 12 months within the framework of the secretary-general's mission of good offices," the U.N. spokesman said.

"Professor Han has consistently demonstrated great objectivity and a deep understanding of the problems facing the two communities and their respective leaders; he has made a valuable contribution to the search for lasting solutions."

The secretary-general was determined to press ahead with "an intensified effort to bring about a comprehensive settlement in the island" and hoped the current process would lead to direct talks between the two leaders "within the next two or three months," the U.N. spokesman said.
"To this end, he will engage in early consultations to identify a successor to Professor Han."
